title: Time bound for a conditional computation
statement: Let $D$, $M_1$, and $M_2$ be finite-state Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, and let $p$ be a Boolean-valued function on Boolean words. Suppose $D$ computes the one-bit output $[p(x)]$ from every input $x$ within $T_0(|x|)$ steps, and $M_1$ and $M_2$ compute $f_1(x)$ and $f_2(x)$ within $T_1(|x|)$ and $T_2(|x|)$ steps, respectively. Then the timed conditional controller computes $f_1(x)$ when $p(x)$ is true and $f_2(x)$ otherwise, within $5\bigl(T_0(|x|)+\max(T_1(|x|),T_2(|x|))+1\bigr)$ steps for every input $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $D,M_1,M_2$ are finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet
